newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Swedish mortgage bank defends planned merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swedish mortgage bank defends planned merger.

text.p: The board of Swedish mortgage bank Stadshypotek, stung by a minister's criticism, hit back on Wednesday saying a planned merger with insurer Skandia would benefit all its shareholders.
In an open letter to Finance Minister Erik Asbrink, the board members said they had no intention of resigning.

Asbrink had said on Monday he had no confidence in the board of Stadshypotek -- Sweden's largest mortgage lender, with about one third of the market, accusing them of failing to consult the state -- which is a shareholder -- about the merger plan.
"The Stadshypotek management maintains that a deal with Skandia benefits everyone, but we do not think it safeguards our interests," Asbrink repeated on Wednesday.
Although Asbrink did not specifically ask the bank's board to step down, he said people might draw their own conclusions.
As a substantial minority shareholder with a 34 percent stake, the government could demand an extraordinary general meeting to discuss the issue.
The finance ministry had said on Saturday it would sell the Stadshypotek stake through a controlled auction, so as to make the maximum money for taxpayers.
Stadshypotek's board said on Wednesday it had tried to discuss the merger with the ministry, but had been rebuffed.

It said the board had to act in the interest of all shareholders, and the fact that one owner intended to dispose of its stake was no reason to delay measures the board considered to be "for the benefit of the shareholders and company".
For these reasons board members had agreed not to offer their resignations, the statement concluded.
The merger of Stadshypotek and Skandia would create the biggest financial institution in the Nordic region with total assets of 500 billion crowns ($75 billion).
Hans Jacobson, a senior ministry official, said on Wednesday that the auction procedure was going ahead.
"We are just starting the process where interested parties are invited to make a bid. We have contacted a handful, but there is no rush, no deadline," he said.
Skandia's bid would be analysed along with others, Jacobson said, adding that the government would prefer for any bid to include an offer to buy out Stadshypotek's entire share capital.

Skandia managing director Bjorn Wolrath believes the state will have difficulty attracting offers for the Stadshypotek state worth more than Skandia's eight billion crowns, a view endorsed by the financial magazine Affarsvarlden.
Newspapers on Wednesday said S-E-Banken, Handelsbanken, and state-controlled Nordbanken were likely bidders, adding that GE Capital might also be interested.
Jacobson declined to identify possible bidders.
Skandia will hold a roadshow in New York on Monday to explain plans for the merger, spokesman Anders Lundblad said.

Credit rating agency Standard & Poor's, affirming its assessment of debt by both Skandia and Stadshypotek on Wednesday, said it believed the companies to be a good match financially, Skandia's potential volatility being balanced by the mortgage bank's steady earnings.
Analysts contacted by Reuters were sceptical about the 1.2 billion crowns synergy savings which the two firms said they would realise, and even about the suitability of the partners.
Some tipped Handelsbanken as the best suitor for Stadshypotek in economic terms, but wondered whether the carefully-managed commercial bank wanted to pay a premium.
The Social Democratic government might favour tying Stadshypotek to state-controlled Nordbanken, others said. ($1=6.666 Swedish Crown)
